seo.title: Marine R&D, CFD Simulation & Measurement | LASAN MARINE
seo.description: R&D for ship-design questions involving hydrodynamics, CFD, structures, vibration, propulsion, measurement and applied research.

fields.headline: For the technical questions that remain open
fields.lead: We use CFD, structural analysis, measurement, testing and data analysis to investigate questions around hydrodynamics, structures, vibration and propulsion. The method follows the question—not the other way around.

fields.heading: Every research problem starts with a question worth answering
fields.intro: R&D does not replace the calculations that belong in normal ship design. It is where we investigate a hypothesis, study a phenomenon, develop a method or compare a model with measured data when the question calls for a dedicated investigation.

items.problem: I need to compare two geometries or operating conditions
items.context: Visual inspection alone cannot show which change is driving resistance, flow behaviour or hydrodynamic loading.
items.solution: CFD lets us compare cases on the same basis, identify the direction and scale of change, and locate areas that deserve closer attention before the design is revised.

items.problem: I need to understand cavitation risk or unfavourable flow around a propeller
items.context: Cavitation and local flow behaviour depend strongly on geometry, velocity and operating condition, making them difficult to assess from external observation alone.
items.solution: Simulation can reveal pressure distribution, velocity fields and potentially adverse regions, giving the project better evidence before deciding whether a design change is justified.

items.problem: I need to investigate stress, vibration or structural strength
items.context: Critical regions may only appear under a specific load case, restraint condition or operating state.
items.solution: Structural analysis helps compare operating states, identify high-stress regions and examine vibration behaviour before a design change is made.

items.problem: I need measured data to check a design or model
items.context: Geometric deviation and real operating parameters can materially affect a calculation or simulation result.
items.solution: Measurement provides data that can be compared with design values and model outputs, helping us judge whether the model represents the real system closely enough for the conclusion being drawn.

fields.heading: Current research areas: hydrodynamics, structures and measurement

items.name: Flow Simulation & Hydrodynamics
items.desc: Simulation of flow around hulls, propellers and rudders to compare designs and investigate resistance, loading and other hydrodynamic behaviour.

items.name: Structures, Propulsion & Vibration
items.desc: Stress, deformation and vibration analysis for strength checks, operating-state comparison and investigation of areas that may require design attention.

items.name: Measurement & Model Validation
items.desc: Real-world measurement for geometry and operating parameters, used to compare design intent, calculation models and workshop or field conditions.

children.name: Comparison of measured data with simulation models

fields.heading: A simulation result is only as useful as the model behind it
fields.content: We pay close attention to geometry, mesh quality, boundary conditions and convergence because each can change the result. Where measured data or a reliable reference is available, we use it to challenge the model and make the limits of the conclusion explicit.

fields.heading: Common questions about simulation, measurement and research
fields.intro: Every investigation has a different level of uncertainty, data availability and validation need. The questions below explain how we choose methods and what the resulting work can look like.

items.title: I have a technical problem but do not know whether it needs simulation or measurement. Can you help define the approach?
items.content: Yes. Start with the phenomenon, hypothesis or decision you need to investigate. We will review the available data and discuss whether simulation, measurement, data analysis or a combination makes the most sense.

items.title: Does every simulation need measured data for validation?
items.content: Not always. The need for measured data depends on the question, the available references and how much confidence the conclusion requires. We will be explicit when real-world data is important to the result.

items.title: What do you deliver from a simulation study?
items.content: Depending on the question, deliverables may include data fields, plots, visualisations, comparison tables and a technical report. We agree the format around how the client needs to use the result.

items.title: Can the free online tools replace project-specific engineering work?
items.content: No. They are intended for quick reference and preliminary checks. Problems with multiple load cases, boundary conditions or design assumptions still need a project-specific calculation or model.

fields.heading: Have a technical question worth investigating?
fields.description: Send us the phenomenon, hypothesis, measured data or design alternatives you are working with. We will review the question and discuss the method, the evidence needed and the most useful form of the final result.
